main_body: Tall brick townhouse with a grey slate mansard roof, a dormer, three floors of windows, a balcony and a green door
top_band: Rows 17-23 are a grey band (L 95-122) under a dark outline row. It stays in the same lightness family as the slate face below it (L about 103), so it reads as part of the front face and not as a roof top.
evidence: The whole building is drawn straight on, like an architectural elevation. The roof is a flat grey slab followed by a vertical slate face with a dormer, and no top slope is visible from above. The scan at x=12, 24 and 35 shows the grey band (L 95-122) and the slate below (L 57-134) are not separated by the required step of 25 L or more. The orange cornice is a thin band the same width as the body. The brick walls, windows and door are flat vertical faces painted on the surface. No horizontal surface is visible from above, so this is a front elevation.

style.evidence: The brick, slate and stone trim carry decent texture, and the 14 colours per tile sit between the two references (18 and 11). There are about 5 shading steps on the brick and the slate. The main problem is the outline: 90% of the dark edge pixels are neutral near-black, against 7-9% on the references, so it looks like a sticker outline and not the dark tone of the neighbouring material. The distinct colour count of 49 is also low next to the richer reference, which has 185. The look is thinner and more outlined than Beodeul, so it fails.
